question.text: The position of an object traveling along a straight path varies with time according to the relation x = 32t − (8/3)t³, where the coordinate x is in metres and time t is in seconds. Determine its acceleration at the moment it momentarily comes to a stop.
conditions: x is in metres and t in seconds
evaluated at the instant the particle is at rest

solution.approach: Differentiate the position function to get velocity, find the time the particle is at rest, then differentiate again to get acceleration at that time.

steps.text: Differentiate the position function to get the velocity.
Set the velocity to zero and solve for the physically valid (positive) time.
Differentiate the velocity to get acceleration, then evaluate it at t = 2 s.

common_mistakes.text: Solving 32 − 8t² = 0 and taking the negative root t = −2 s instead of the physical t = 2 s, giving a(−2) = 32 ms⁻².
